articles.title: Himachal: Lottery revival fails to draw big players
articles.description: The Himachal Pradesh Government’s much-publicised plan to revive its lottery business after nearly three decades has hit an early roadblock, with the tender failing to attract a strong response from established lottery operators. With hardly any bids received by the September 14 deadline, the Finance Department has extended the last date for submitting bids by [...]

articles.title: BHEL Leadership Reset Ahead of 2027: Why Succession Will Matter for India’s Power and Manufacturing Ecosystem
articles.description: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited is approaching an important leadership inflection point. By the beginning of March 2027, India's public-sector engineering major could have a substantially different leadership team at the top. Chairman and Managing Director K Sadashiv Murthy is scheduled to superannuate on February 28, 2027, while Director Power Tajinder Gupta is also expected to retire on the same date. Director Engineering, Research and Development S M Ramanathan is scheduled to superannuate a month earlier, on January 31, 2027. With CMD K Sadashiv Murthy and two key functional directors approaching superannuation, BHEL faces one of its most significant management transitions in recent years. The timing is crucial: the engineering giant is carrying an order book of around ₹2.4 lakh crore and has returned to strong revenue and profit growth. Meanwhile, the position of Director Human Resources has remained vacant since March 2026, with Tajinder Gupta currently holding additional charge of the HR portfolio. On the surface, these may appear to be routine leadership changes associated with superannuation in a large Central Public Sector Enterprise. But the timing gives the developments much greater significance. BHEL is entering the transition at a moment when its business momentum, project pipeline, diversification strategy and role in India's energy security ambitions are all expanding simultaneously. The leadership change, therefore, is not simply about who occupies the corner office at BHEL House. It could influence how effectively one of India's largest engineering enterprises converts an enormous order pipeline into revenues, profitability, technological capability and opportunities for thousands of suppliers, contractors and MSMEs. A Major Transition at the Top K Sadashiv Murthy assumed charge as BHEL's Chairman and Managing Director on November 1, 2023. His present appointment runs up to February 28, 2027 or until further government orders. The Public Enterprises Selection Board process for identifying his successor has already been initiated, with the Ministry of Heavy Industries publishing the CMD vacancy in May 2026. Similarly, Tajinder Gupta, who joined BHEL's board as Director Power in September 2023, has emerged as an important operational leader during a period of renewed activity in India's thermal power sector. Following the departure of Krishna Kumar Thakur from the HR portfolio in March 2026, Gupta was also given additional responsibility as Director Human Resources. BHEL's official records confirm that Thakur relinquished charge on March 19, 2026 and Gupta subsequently assumed the additional HR responsibility. S M Ramanathan represents another strategically important position in the leadership structure. An IIT Madras-trained mechanical engineer with decades of experience across BHEL's manufacturing, engineering, R&D and operational ecosystem, Ramanathan assumed charge as Director Engineering, Research and Development on April 30, 2025. His experience spans hydro turbines, steam turbines, switchgear, digital technologies, production, project functions and finance. The near-simultaneous transition across CMD, Power, R&D and HR functions creates an unusual concentration of leadership change. That is what makes succession particularly important. Why the Timing Matters: BHEL Is Carrying a ₹2.4 Lakh Crore Order Book The leadership transition is taking place against a dramatically improved operating backdrop. BHEL reported turnover of approximately ₹32,350 crore for FY2025-26, representing growth of around 18 percent over the previous year. The company received orders worth approximately ₹75,000 crore during the year, taking its outstanding order book to roughly ₹2.4 lakh crore at the end of FY2025-26. Power-sector orders alone were worth approximately ₹59,000 crore, while around ₹16,000 crore came from industrial businesses including transportation, transmission, defence, process industries and industrial equipment. BHEL also commissioned or synchronised approximately 8.9 GW of power capacity during FY2025-26. These numbers fundamentally change the leadership discussion. For a company with such a large order book, the challenge is no longer confined to winning projects. The real test is execution . A ₹2.4 lakh crore order pipeline requires extensive coordination across engineering, procurement, manufacturing, project management, construction, vendors, logistics, working capital and customer interfaces. Any prolonged leadership vacuum across key operating functions could potentially slow decision-making at precisely the stage when execution velocity becomes critical. Conversely, a well-managed transition could allow the next leadership team to inherit one of the strongest opportunity pipelines BHEL has seen in years. Profitability Has Also Started Improving Another important factor is BHEL's improving financial performance. In the April-June quarter of FY2026-27, BHEL reported consolidated net profit of approximately ₹376.7 crore compared with a loss of around ₹455.5 crore during the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Revenue from operations increased more than 40 percent year-on-year to approximately ₹7,698 crore. Significantly, the company's power business returned to profitability during the quarter. Power-segment revenue grew to about ₹5,919.5 crore, compared with ₹3,898.9 crore during the corresponding period a year earlier. This means BHEL's next leadership is unlikely to inherit a company merely attempting a turnaround. It could inherit a company entering the execution phase of that turnaround . And these are very different management challenges. Winning orders requires competitiveness. Executing a massive backlog requires project discipline, supply-chain management, working-capital control and rapid decision-making. The Next CMD Will Have Five Strategic Priorities The incoming leadership will potentially need to simultaneously manage five major priorities. First will be order execution. The company's huge order book must translate into predictable revenue and cash flow. EPC execution, vendor coordination, project closures and timely delivery will remain critical. Second will be diversification beyond conventional power equipment. BHEL has been expanding capabilities across nuclear energy, defence, transportation, transmission, hydrogen, coal gasification and other emerging technologies. The company itself has stated that it is building capabilities in areas including defence, aerospace, urban mobility, rail transportation, hydrogen and carbon capture. Third will be technology. The retirement of the Director Engineering and R&D assumes significance because BHEL is simultaneously trying to strengthen indigenous technology capabilities. The company has recently pursued partnerships in areas such as electrolyser technologies while positioning itself for emerging opportunities associated with India's clean-energy transition. BHEL announced strategic tie-ups during 2026 relating to both alkaline and PEM electrolyser systems. Fourth will be people and organisational transformation. The HR director's position has already required an additional-charge arrangement. With several senior executives approaching superannuation, succession planning below board level will also become important. For an organisation with extensive engineering and manufacturing capabilities accumulated over decades, preserving institutional knowledge while bringing younger leadership into decision-making will be essential. Fifth will be supply-chain development. And this is where the transition becomes particularly relevant to India's MSME ecosystem. Why BHEL's Leadership Transition Matters to MSMEs BHEL is much more than a large PSU operating in isolation. Behind its power plants, industrial equipment and infrastructure projects exists a significant ecosystem of equipment manufacturers, fabricators, engineering firms, component suppliers, service providers, contractors and MSMEs. A growing BHEL order book can therefore produce a multiplier effect throughout Indian manufacturing. The company's procurement system actively engages suppliers across numerous manufacturing and project categories. BHEL also encourages MSME suppliers to register on TReDS platforms for receivables financing and operates centralised procurement arrangements for several project requirements. For MSMEs, three issues will consequently be important during the leadership transition: Continuity of procurement: Large project pipelines require predictable tendering and purchase orders. Faster vendor payments: MSMEs supplying complex engineering projects depend heavily on timely cash flows. Vendor capability development: As BHEL enters higher-technology businesses such as nuclear, defence, hydrogen and advanced transmission, Indian SMEs will need support to meet increasingly sophisticated quality and certification requirements. This represents an opportunity. Instead of viewing vendors simply as suppliers, the next BHEL leadership could treat MSMEs as strategic manufacturing partners. Such an approach would strengthen both BHEL's execution capability and India's broader objective of creating deeper domestic manufacturing supply chains. Energy Security Makes BHEL Strategically Important BHEL's relevance also needs to be viewed within India's changing energy landscape. While renewable energy capacity is expanding rapidly, India's electricity requirement continues to grow. Thermal generation remains an important part of the country's energy security architecture, while nuclear power is expected to assume a larger role over the coming decades. BHEL is positioned across several parts of this transition. It retains a strong presence in thermal power equipment while simultaneously expanding into transmission, nuclear technologies, rail transportation, defence and new-energy technologies. Its own strategic outlook has identified nuclear energy as an important opportunity, especially as India works toward significantly expanding nuclear generation capacity over the longer term. The challenge for the next leadership will therefore not be to choose simply between conventional and clean energy. It will be to position BHEL across India's entire evolving energy architecture . Leadership Continuity Will Be Closely Watched The government and Public Enterprises Selection Board have already initiated processes relating to future leadership positions. The CMD vacancy was advertised during May 2026, while the post of Director Power was subsequently advertised in June. The Director HR vacancy had also been advertised earlier following the position becoming vacant in March. That advance planning becomes important because large engineering companies benefit from continuity. Strategic decisions made today can affect projects that will remain under execution for five or even ten years. Power plants, transmission systems, nuclear equipment and industrial projects do not operate according to quarterly timelines. They require institutional consistency. SMEStreet Perspective: This Is More Than a PSU Appointment Story The forthcoming leadership changes at BHEL should therefore not be viewed merely as another round of PSU appointments. They arrive at a defining stage for the company. BHEL has regained revenue momentum. Its order book has expanded dramatically. Its power business is showing signs of stronger financial performance. At the same time, the company is attempting to move deeper into new technology-led areas. The next CMD and functional directors will have to protect this momentum. The ultimate measure of success will not be the size of the order book inherited by the new leadership, but how effectively that order book gets converted into completed projects, revenues, profitability and stronger domestic manufacturing capabilities. For India's MSMEs, the transition carries another message. A stronger, faster and more technologically ambitious BHEL could become an even larger anchor customer for India's engineering SMEs, component manufacturers and industrial service providers. That makes leadership continuity at BHEL relevant not only to shareholders and policymakers but also to thousands of enterprises operating throughout India's industrial supply chain. As February 2027 approaches, the focus will naturally remain on who succeeds K Sadashiv Murthy and the other retiring directors. But the more important question will be what mandate the next leadership receives. If the mandate combines disciplined execution, technology development, supplier ecosystem expansion and aggressive diversification, BHEL's approaching leadership transition could mark not simply a change of guard — but the beginning of the company's next growth cycle.
